clue.text: Feeling good about tobacco

parts.note: to be about something, as in what are you about, is to be up to it
snuff is powdered tobacco taken through the nose

explanation.surface: A smoker feels cheerful about their tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in proper health or form, so feeling good fits as a predicate phrase.

clue.text: Out of bed, attempt to get a result

parts.note: up means risen, out of bed
a shot is a try, an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone rises early and tries to get something done.
explanation.definitionFit: The final outcome or consequence of something, a synonym of result.

clue.text: On a Dutch trip, travel is risky

indicators.note: trip is read as a stumble, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: go means travel

explanation.surface: Travelling on a trip to Holland is dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means precarious, with the outcome uncertain.

clue.text: Bullock takes time creating space on vessel

indicators.note: takes means is joined by, so the time word follows

parts.note: a steer is a young castrated bull, a bullock
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A bullock takes a while making room on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheapest accommodation on a passenger ship, a part of the vessel's space.

clue.text: Heartless remark I found in several organs

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: to utter is to say, to remark

explanation.surface: A cruel comment is found among the organs.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the Latin word for the womb, so several such organs.

clue.text: Is the woman's husband at first following angler?

indicators.note: at first puts the following letter at the start

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
her is the possessive for the woman
man as in man and wife, a husband

explanation.surface: A question whether a wife's husband was the first person to go after an angler.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who catches fish, of which an angler with rod and line is one kind.

clue.text: More than one tea dance

indicators.note: more than one is read as a doubling, so the tea word appears twice

parts.note: cha, or char, is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A tea dance with several cups served.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American ballroom dance, an example of a dance.

clue.text: Pirate's bed

definitions.meaning: to pirate is to copy another's work unlawfully, to plagiarise

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to copy illicitly and also a small bed for an infant.

clue.text: Society figure in plane I hauled out to kill

indicators.note: hauled out means pulled away, so the letter I is removed

parts.note: a triangle is a figure in plane geometry

explanation.surface: A society figure on an aeroplane is dragged out to be murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill by choking, a specific way of killing.

clue.text: Come into their refurbished home first

indicators.note: first places the word for home ahead of the rest

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: refurbished means done up anew, so the letters of their are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes possession of a house that the previous owners have done up.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into money or property is to receive it as an heir, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Upset, they use the rest

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of they use are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being troubled, a couple take a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal slang for sleep, which is a kind of rest taken with the eyes closed.

clue.text: Sinuous creature providing firm support

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A snaking animal gives a firm grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A venomous hooded snake, an example of a creature that moves in curves.

clue.text: Theories' weight represented in a different way

indicators.note: represented is read as re-presented, laid out again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Scientific ideas carry a different significance when put another way.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means differently or in another manner, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Working for a degree, here?

definitions.meaning: ... a subject is the British way of saying studying it at university
An English town with a university, so a place where one might study

explanation.definitionFit: Studying a subject at a British university is called reading it; the town also hosts a university.

clue.text: Novelty in pub given enthusiastic reception

parts.note: an inn is a pub
an ovation is applause, an enthusiastic reception

explanation.surface: Something new in a pub earns warm applause.
explanation.definitionFit: A new idea or method, a novelty, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Member of the royal household's grand accommodation

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
room means space or lodging, accommodation

explanation.surface: A palace servant is given a fine apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A groom of the chamber or of the stole is an officer of the British royal household.

clue.text: Retainer puts work first, though not initially attentive to detail

indicators.note: first places the trimmed work word ahead of the retainer
not initially means without the first letter

parts.note: a job is work
a retainer is a servant kept in a household

explanation.surface: A servant prioritises his work, though not at the outset, while noting details.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick to notice things, a synonym for attentive to detail.

clue.text: Fence, and take evasive action

definitions.meaning: a row of bushes forming a boundary, a living fence
to avoid committing oneself, to equivocate

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a bushy boundary and, as a verb, means dodging a straight answer.

clue.text: Endless forms of publicity are soporific

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off each word

parts.note: hype is overblown promotion, a form of publicity
a notice is a public announcement, another form of publicity

explanation.surface: Unending advertising has a sleepy effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' acts on both forms of publicity: HYPE and NOTICE each lose their final E, leaving HYP and NOTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that induces sleep, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Clubs involved in function in the past

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so the clubs letter goes inside the function

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: Golf clubs played a part in some former social function.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means ago or before now, as in long since.

clue.text: Most winsome saint (little) put on trial

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A very charming little saint stands trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of an adjective meaning charming or appealing, matching the superlative definition.

clue.text: Note fresh source of physical strength

parts.note: si is a variant name for te, the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
new means fresh

explanation.surface: A doctor's note talks of a new start for someone's physical vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is literally what powers muscle, and figuratively stands for strength itself.

clue.text: Will's authentication Robert's got his head around

indicators.note: around means placed about, so the head word wraps the name

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
Rob is a short form of Robert

explanation.surface: Someone named Robert has finally understood how a will is validated.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text had a stray 'st'; the page has none. 'Got his head around' reads as understood, but the head word goes around ROB.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal process by which a court confirms a will is genuine before it is executed.

clue.text: I tramp around a hollow

indicators.note: around means moved about, so the letters of I tramp are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vagrant walks round a hollow in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollow under the shoulder where the arm joins the body.

clue.text: The purpose of sleeping out here?

definitions.meaning: camping out means sleeping in a tent, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: The word means aim or purpose, and split in two it says where a camper sleeps.

clue.text: Eve had to create a disturbance

definitions.meaning: Eve, the first woman, had to bring up her son Cain
to kick up a fuss, make trouble

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means make a loud fuss; literally it describes Eve bringing up her son Cain.

clue.text: Topping one hundred is not good for starters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: for starters means the opening letters of these words are taken

explanation.surface: Putting a top of more than a hundred runs is a poor beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar coating spread over a cake, a kind of topping.

clue.text: Headless? Na, that would cause disgust

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium

explanation.surface: Someone is so appalled by the word Na that they would lose their head.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatred or loathing directed at someone, close enough to disgust as a noun.

clue.text: My method of investing yen

parts.note: an ISA is an individual savings account, a British tax-free way to invest
Y is the symbol for yen, the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: Someone describes their own way of putting money into Japanese currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, so the old-fashioned interjection matches.

clue.text: List some quite miserable contents

indicators.note: contents means what is held within, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to note down a few rather unhappy items.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out item by item, a verb synonym for listing.

clue.text: Romance that covers this sex appeal bringing two men together

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal
Al is a short man's name
Ian is another man's name

explanation.surface: A love affair with an attractive figure unites two men.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole stretch before the dash: Romance is the language family that covers this one.
explanation.definitionFit: A language descended from Latin, so the Romance family includes it.

clue.text: Drunken fool said to be closely integrated

indicators.note: said to be signals the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: tight means drunk and a nit is a fool

explanation.surface: An inebriated idiot is closely bound up with his friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a group bonded closely together, as in a close community.
